findings.explanation: From the root README and registrations I could trace the analysis, two data modules, algorithm, comparison data and container. Loader paths establish how those modules are consumed. The private acquisition-source submodule is not read by this result-producing analysis, so its unresolved location does not defeat this scope boundary.

Both executable analysis and its inputs are explicitly referenced. This includes comparison data nested under REMoDNaV and the hard-coded comparison summaries whose source is identified in the script. The omitted payload bytes are an inspection constraint, not missing object references.

The root exposes an image recipe and registration, analysis flags, and dependency declarations; algorithm parameters and intentional defaults are inspectable. Mutable package resolution concerns version precision, not whether these dependencies and settings are represented.

The linked module texts establish several distinct license declarations. The label-module inventory and README supply no corresponding declaration, which independently prevents the universal anchor. Uninspected image contents should remain an unresolved license-coverage question, not a claim that licenses are physically absent there.

I checked the root tree: its three gitlinks identify exact raw-data, labels and algorithm commits, and the image manifest gives content digests. Tracked scripts, settings and outputs also have Git object identities. No floating selection was found for the consumed research components; build-time dependency resolution remains a separate issue.

The root Git tree composes subdataset commits with normal files, while annex pointers retain large-content identities in the same tracking structure. This supports an integrated state description even though payload availability cannot be tested.

The cached root and linked-module histories show actors, dates and change descriptions across code, data, environment and manuscript/figure classes. The explicit manual flowchart correction is modification provenance, although it is not programmatic execution provenance.

The historical DataLad records actually contain commands, inputs, outputs and exit values, so these are stronger than script definitions. Coverage remains partial: quality_stats is outside the recorded CLI path, and earlier figure records have empty input declarations. I found no basis for the all-steps anchor.

The main container run is attached to a concrete tree and declares the image as an extra input; the recorded tree pins the same three subdatasets. The label run has no captured environment identity. Image-build and conversion records also leave host/build-tool state less precise than the all-executions anchor requires.

A read-only Git probe confirmed the annotated tag points to the analysis commit and contains an armored PGP signature. Neither the inspected documentation nor the supplied tag identifies a usable signer-key distribution and identity-verification procedure. The binary zero is supported without claiming the tag is unsigned or cryptographically invalid.

The root gives clone, rerun and manuscript commands and explains automatic download of data and image content. The run record enumerates nested comparison data and the raw/derived data patterns. This is sufficient procedural acquisition evidence within the declared consumed-input scope; no successful retrieval is inferred.

The container sequence and installation links provide substantial setup guidance, but the highest anchor is stated more strongly than the frozen evidence establishes. The linked installation pages are not in the package, and P-01 itself identifies non-root Docker service access as an implicit essential prerequisite. The adapter explicitly notes this undocumented assumption. The assessment should explain why that initialization gap does not also affect operational setup completeness.
findings.suggested_correction: Retain the installation links as evidence, but qualify what was inspected. Reconcile A-02 with the identified P-01 prerequisite; use anchor 2 if setting up Docker access remains an essential recipient decision, or supply the explicit setup route supporting anchor 3.

findings.explanation: The central run and PDF destination are clear, but they do not provide a complete end-to-end sequence for all numerical and figure content. There is an inline instruction to add quality_stats, so it is inaccurate to treat that calculation as wholly undocumented; nevertheless the flowchart reference code and manual assembly remain outside an unambiguous reproduction sequence. The limited rating is defensible for the full figure scope.

The supplied executable clone/rerun sequence and concrete input declarations assemble the nested comparison files, event tables, gaze data and image. The manuscript sources and figure assets are in the root tree. I did not find another required assembly step for consuming these deposited inputs.

The main analysis and rendering are executable, but the figure-generation scope is broader. flowchart_figs is explicitly reference-only, closes figures without saving them, and its helper returns only b although the caller unpacks b and a. Manual flowchart assembly/correction is documented historically. These are concrete reasons not to award complete executable coverage; merely needing to call quality_stats would be a weaker reason.

The root supplies a replay command tied to captured analysis inputs and an image. The linked label-producing record exposes a command but does not preserve its original environment. Accordingly a replay mechanism is demonstrated for part of the provenance, without establishing reconstruction of every recorded execution context.

Input datasets, algorithm source, analysis script, container, image assets and manuscript have identifiable responsibilities and separable locations. Distinct roles do not require separate repositories, so the mixture of root files and subdatasets is consistent with the top anchor.

The algorithm has a documented CLI, but the paper analysis bypasses an abstract data interface and names the algorithm test-data internals directly. Subject and layout assumptions also occur inside consumers. Independent Git selection does not by itself make these module replacements confined to declared configuration boundaries.

Separating the algorithm and raw-data modules preserves their own license declarations. No comparable module-level declaration is supplied for the event-label dataset. Thus some independent scopes are clear and others unresolved, matching anchor 2 without assuming the root license governs every linked component.

The modules carry identifiable terms, but I found no object-specific record explaining compatibility when these materials or image components are combined. Anchor 1 accommodates this listing-without-combination-handling evidence; it is not a finding of legal incompatibility.

The rationale expressly says that access conditions cannot be determined for all relevant material. M-05 anchor 0 explicitly covers that state. The assessment instead treats the lack of support for the positive uniform/mixed-access anchors as a reason for null, overlooking the applicable zero anchor. This is an anchor-specific judgment of non-demonstration, not proof of restricted access or a retrieval failure.
findings.suggested_correction: Assign 0 under the indeterminate-access branch and retain the evidence limitation. Use an observation that describes the inspected access information rather than implying an attempted remote access failure. Update completion reporting; D-01 can remain unanswered.

findings.explanation: The selected subdataset states, relative paths, environment registration and Make/manuscript connections jointly specify the assembly. Hard-coded paths weaken replaceability under M-02 but still make the existing composition explicit. The unused private acquisition source is not necessary to reconstruct this consumption boundary.

The README names tools, supported platforms and approximate downloads/runtime. The adapter explicitly assumes Docker on PATH usable by a non-root user and notes that this should be documented. That concrete host prerequisite supports the partial rating; no extra unobserved hardware requirement is needed to justify it.

The active analysis uses repository-relative data paths, the adapter derives its bind mount from the current directory and computes user/group IDs, and Python selection has a configuration override. The obsolete Condor scripts are not the recorded compute_all path and should not automatically lower the active procedure rating.

The inspected imports are covered by the recipe and linked package dependencies, including numerical, plotting, statistical, and rendering tools. DataLad inside the container is optional because inputs are retrieved outside it and the script supplies a fallback. The evidence supports dependency coverage for the current result-producing route, not a reconstruction of every historical environment.

The recipe, image registration/manifest and algorithm dependency definition are tracked at concrete root/module revisions. The criterion is binary and asks whether definitions are versioned; moving package indexes do not turn these tracked definitions into an unversioned specification.

The environment is represented in formats Docker and the registered adapter can consume, and compatible platforms are documented. The adapter resolves a content-derived image identity rather than relying on the mutable latest name. This supports specification capability while payload availability and exact rebuilds remain untested/separately assessed.

The adapter unquestionably starts a new docker run from the identified image. However the claim of a fresh temporary HOME for every invocation is not established: /tmp is the bind-mounted working directory, HOME is always /tmp/dockertmp, and cleanup runs only after a successful make. On failure that directory remains; the next mkdir can fail while the semicolon still permits make to run with the retained HOME. A fresh container therefore does not guarantee fresh effective user-environment state.
findings.suggested_correction: Qualify the successful-run lifecycle and explicitly resolve the retained HOME case before asserting the whole highest anchor. If retaining 3 for immutable container freshness, explain the interpretation and register that mutable user-site/configuration state is handled under E-03 rather than claiming it is always recreated.

findings.explanation: Results are written into the bind-mounted dataset, and DataLad records live outside the container. The adapter passes --rm, so successful computation does not require preserving its mutable container. The assessment correctly limits HOME cleanup to success; failure residue is a qualification to environment freshness, not evidence that required outputs are lost on disposal.

The cloned tracked state and declared data inputs make an initial workspace identifiable, but the bind mount is persistent and globs can consume added files. The cleanup targets remove build/cache products rather than enforce a pristine dataset, and a failed run can retain dockertmp. Anchor 2 is supportable with an explicit recipient reset; automatic isolation is not established.

The manifest and annex metadata document intended-state references and retrieval locations, but the cohort deliberately excludes the payloads and forbids access tests. No observed unavailable version or absent route justifies a low anchor, and complete successful intended-state provision is not established. Null is an appropriate unresolved judgment here, unlike M-05 whose zero explicitly addresses indeterminate conditions.

The raw-data and algorithm modules expose deposit/DOI routes, while the image metadata names only one payload host. Exact hashes prevent unnoticed substitution but cannot recover absent bytes. I found no supplied preservation commitment or independently recoverable complete bundle for every required module, so the conservative rating is defensible. The annex availability record should be cited directly for the single-host claim.

Debian is selected by a moving tag, apt packages are unpinned and only four pip packages have exact versions. These include top-level system dependencies, so the partially pinned top-level-dependency anchor is not wholly satisfied. Keeping an identified image does not freeze the recipe inputs.

The inspected texts identify CC BY 4.0, MIT, PDDL and GPLv3 clearly enough to resolve their terms. The event-label module has no comparable governing reference in its supplied inventory. That gap suffices for anchor 2; this review does not infer undisclosed licenses inside omitted container layers.

The assessed tree fixes code, inputs, settings, assets and container representation as a joint selection. The old signed results tag and current tree are distinguishable, including the later OCI conversion; their difference does not make the assessed root selection float. This criterion properly remains separate from retrieval and bitwise agreement with the original publication.

The image build and later format-conversion records provide source and transformation context, but no supplied artifact attestation authenticates producer and build source for the distributed image. The signed result tag does not alone establish that artifact-origin verification route, particularly for the later OCI representation. Binary zero is justified as non-demonstration.

limitations: Inspection-only review of frozen cohort remodnav-e3c6253bced7; manifest SHA-256 was verified. No network calls, scientific execution, container builds or payload acquisition occurred.

Binary figures, container layers/config payloads and annex data are excluded. Their current availability, actual contents, licensing inside layers and numerical reproducibility were not verified. Absence from this package is not an observed retrieval failure.

Root discovery proceeded through README, tracked files and explicit subdataset links. The external Docker adapter was inspected only in the supplied versioned cache; its release-tag URL is not a commit pin, so findings cite the frozen cache hash. Signature presence was inspected without cryptographic signer verification.

All 36 native responses and their anchors were checked. Native validation passed, including the exact rubric hash. The supplied assessment has 34 answered criteria out of the fixed denominator of 36; both nulls are retained in its provisional total, weights are all one, and binary anchors are valid. No arithmetic or denominator inconsistency was found. The M-05 correction would change completion without changing its zero contribution.

The current consuming analysis/rendering route is distinguished from historical label production and unused legacy Condor/acquisition paths. The assessment should make this scope distinction explicit wherever claiming complete environment coverage.
Only the assigned anonymized assessment was consulted. No other assessments, reviews, examples or peer outputs were read. Agreement is an independent evidential judgment, not human approval.
